Hi Ella — great meeting you. Quick recap + concrete next steps below.

Recap/Recommendations:
- Recommended models to benchmark (initial slate):
  * redwood-embed-v1 (1024d) — tuned for semantic search / clinical vocab, best cost/quality balance
  * open-embed-large (1536d) — higher-dimensional baseline for matching your current ada baseline
  * redwood-embed-compact (512d, quantization-friendly) — for ANNs where index size matters

- Rationale: redwood-embed-v1 tends to improve MAP@10 by ~4–7% vs. generic open models on domain corpora we’ve tested; compact 512d embeddings are often within ~2–3% MAP but reduce index size by ~40%.

Attached artifacts I’m sharing now:

3) If results align, run a drift check across specialties (split by service line) and recommend retrain/re-index cadence.

Thanks — adding a few technical notes so everyone is aligned on metrics, drift detection, and dimensionality tradeoffs.

Metrics we recommend for the POC (compute per-slice and global):
- Recall@10 (primary retrieval recall)
- MAP@10 (mean avg precision at 10)
- nDCG@10 (rank-aware quality)
- Median retrieval latency (ms) at target QPS and 95th percentile
- Index size (GB) and cost estimate (storage + memory for ANN)

Notes on dimensionality and quantization:
- 1024d (redwood-embed-v1) is a good balance for clinical text — yields strong MAP and maintains reasonable index sizes.
- 1536d (open-embed-large) may marginally improve MAP but increases ANN memory by ~50% in our tests.
- 512d compact embeddings often perform well after fine-tuning/semantic alignment; consider using them for cold indexes or mobile clients.
- Quantization (8-bit/4-bit) can reduce storage but watch for small regressions in MAP (~1–4% depending on data). We recommend evaluating quantized variants as a follow-up step, not in the initial baseline.

Drift detection suggestions:
- Compute centroid shift per specialty (cosine centroid) and monitor KL divergence on score distributions monthly.
- Keep a rolling eval set (5k labeled pairs) for continuous MAP checks; trigger retrain/reindex if MAP drops >5% absolute.

Operational ask: please share a sanitized 50k sample (we only need de-identified text + query/label pairs) in the shared drive. We’ll run the baseline eval and post the results in the notebook.

I’ve attached the notebook and the quick-run CSV Marcus produced. Marcus — I’ll sync with you after the first run to decide if we should add the compact 512d variant.

Thanks,
